source.title: Intersection of Parallels as an Early Stopping Criterion
source.authors: Ali Vardasbi; M. de Rijke; Mostafa Dehghani

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test performance across training epochs and reports an epoch-wise trajectory, but does not use the original double-descent analysis.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 is the direct result bearing on an epoch-wise curve: the text says test performance continues to decrease after the L-curve corner. The paper's comparisons of early-stopping methods, and its variations in model size and training-data selection, do not report test error as a function of model size or sample size around an interpolation threshold, so they are not rows for those versions.
record.test_reason: This is an early-stopping paper. It assumes the classical picture (learn general structure, then overfit) and reports only how well its Cosine-Distance Criterion performs against CV, EB, GD and an oracle. Test-accuracy-over-epoch curves appear only as illustrations of the stopping signal, limited to 500 epochs. No run is designed or long enough to look for a second descent, and no result is framed as bearing on double descent. That makes it T4, not T2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that CDC, which stops training when the cosine distance between the weights of two differently seeded instances crosses an L-curve corner (threshold 0.2), needs no validation set. They find it generalizes better on average than CV, EB and gradient disparity across learning rates, and comes close to the oracle for linear and two-layer networks. They conjecture, without verifying, that the instances' intersection marks the start of overfitting. They say deeper networks may need a criterion involving the whole model.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies an early-stopping criterion, not the original double-descent measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity analyses for corner-detection hyperparameters and experiments across learning rates, model sizes, datasets, and loss functions; it does not report these as changes to a double-descent curve.

fits_no_version.finding: In overparameterized linear and two-layer models on MNIST and CIFAR-10 with 50% label noise, test accuracy peaks early and then declines within 500 epochs. The authors give this as the overfitting their stopping rule targets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under heavy label noise, short-horizon training (≤500 epochs) shows a single early test-accuracy peak followed by decline, i.e. classical overfitting, in small linear and two-layer models.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM ’22)
record.problems: The direct epoch-wise evidence is an illustrative trajectory, not a systematic sweep designed to detect a second descent. Relevant plots provide no numerical values in the text, and the Figure 6 test-performance trajectories are not described there.

untested.parts: Long-horizon test error over epochs, including any second descent after the peak. Training is capped at 500 epochs, and the oracle notes the maximum test accuracy falls well before that.
Test error versus model size around the interpolation threshold. The three sizes used are all overparameterized and are not plotted against test error as a size sweep.
Test error versus sample size; not examined.
Label-noise dependence of a peak. The 50% noise level is fixed and used only to induce overfitting.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges V2' label was removed. The study is not designed to detect epoch-wise double descent, and its 500-epoch window cannot rule one out. Absence of a reported second descent in an illustrative figure is not a test result.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not systematically test for a later second descent across training epochs or establish that the trajectory generalizes across models and settings.

The 'continues to decrease' statement covers at most about 500 epochs, so it cannot show whether a later second descent occurs. The study does not test V2, so this row should not carry a challenges verdict.
